# A Complete Guide to Document Automation

## What Does Document Automation Look Like?

### Document Templating

### Document Generation

### Document Management

@context https://schema.org @type Explore our comprehensive guide to mastering document automation with TurboDocx, enhancing efficiency and accuracy across your business. @type @type @type https://www.turbodocx.com/TDAILogo.svg https://www.turbodocx.com/images/blog/document-automation-guide-og.png https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/a-complete-guide-to-document-automation @type @id https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/a-complete-guide-to-document-automation document automation, document generation, document assembly, document templates, workflow automation, business efficiency, document management Guide A Complete Guide to Document Automation Everything You Need to Know About Automating Document Workflows By Nicolas • April 26, 2024 • 8 min read Document automation (also known as document generation or document assembly) is a process that enables users to streamline document workflows . Organizations can use document automation to create and send essential documents to stakeholders faster, improve business efficiencies, and scale productivity. This article will provide a comprehensive guide on what document automation is, why modern businesses need this powerful solution, and how you can use TurboDocx's document automation and templating platform to enhance business operations. What Does Document Automation Look Like? Document automation involves using automation to consolidate and compile data from different sources to create a new, usable document. The documents can include contracts, proposals, statements of work, runbacks, onboarding materials, and more. Here are the general components of document automation software and solutions. Document Templating The first step to document automation involves creating templates for documents your business frequently uses, from master service agreements (MSPs) to term sheets. You can build your own templates, or select pre-existing ones. The automation technology will insert the right text, paragraphs, images, and more into the appropriate section of the document. Document Generation Once the templates are stored onto the platform, the automation software will fill out the necessary information to complete each document. Users can review, edit, and personalize the initial draft of the document as needed. This ability streamlines processes and helps organizations produce new documents at scale. Document Management Users can store all of their documents on document automation systems. These solutions also come with other features, like third-party integrations with data sources, file conversion capabilities, and team collaboration tools. Your organization will be able to reduce the friction of document workflows end-to-end with document automation solutions. Why Your Business Needs Document Automation? Document automation can bring numerous benefits for your business operations for any and all teams. Here's what you can experience in your organization. Efficient Document Workflows Document automation can help your business save time on document creation. Instead of manually copying-and-pasting information from various sources into a new template, you'll be able to automate this process. Document automation solutions include integrations with major third-party data sources, like Salesforce, to help users pull all of the information they need into one place, making document creation a painless process. Error Reduction Automating tedious tasks will also minimize the risk of human error. With automation, teams will be able to deliver more accurate and reliable deliverables faster than ever. Document automation will not only minimize document turnaround times, it can also help teams ensure they never miss another deadline. Standardized Branding Automating the document creation process with templates will ensure the consistency of your team's documents to stakeholders. As the quality and style of documents reflects brand values, you'll be able to build recognition and establish trust and professionalism with consistent documents. High-Quality Production at Scale With document automation, you'll be able to scale high-quality document creation and sharing for all major stakeholders. By automating repetitive tasks, you can ensure quality, consistency, and reliability in your processes. This ability will help your team stay ahead of deadlines and complete deals faster so you can focus more time on other high-growth priorities. Enhanced Client Relationships Respond to client needs more quickly with document automation. By sending high-quality documents like contracts, proposals, or legal documents in a timely manner, you'll be able to build trust and maintain your professional reputation with clients. How Different Teams and Industries Can Use Document Automation? Document automation can be used in any industry from law firms to healthcare services. Industries that depend on accuracy, reliability, and compliance can utilize document automation to reduce risk and maximize operational workflows. Various teams within specific industries can also take advantage of document automation to enhance productivity. From IT teams, legal teams, sales teams, and more, users will be able to generate whatever documents they need more efficiently. What Features to Look for in Document Automation Software When trying to choose the right document automation solution for your business, evaluate your organization's needs. Narrowing down on your business' use cases will help you figure out the best solution for your business. For example, consider features, such as template customization options, what integrations are available, ease of use, pricing options, and more. Choosing a solution based on features that fit your organization's needs will help you choose the right document automation solution. Security & Compliance Automate Documents with TurboDocx Document automation is essential for modern businesses looking to optimize and scale their operations. By understanding the benefits of document automation, you'll be able to choose the right solution for your organization, streamline document workflows, and open up new growth opportunities. Take the first step toward transforming your business with document automation by trying TurboDocx for free. Or, if your business has specific needs, schedule a personalized demo of TurboDocx today. Ready to Transform Your Document Workflows? Start automating your documents today and experience the efficiency of TurboDocx. Try TurboDocx Free Schedule a Demo

@context https://schema.org @type How to Write a Clear and Effective Statement of Work (SOW) Learn how to write a clear, effective Statement of Work (SOW) to manage project scope, expectations, and deliverables. Essential tips for MSPs, project managers, and consultants. @type @type @type https://www.turbodocx.com/TDAILogo.svg https://www.turbodocx.com/images/blog/sow-guide-og.png https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/how-to-write-effective-sow @type @id https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/how-to-write-effective-sow statement of work, SOW, project management, scope management, MSP, consulting, deliverables Best Practices How to Write a Clear and Effective Statement of Work (SOW) From Reddit to Reality: A Complete Guide to SOWs That Prevent Scope Creep By Nicolas • October 10, 2024 • 10 min read So this post went popular on Reddit and I figured it would make sense to move it to our blog as well... Every few moons I see a post on "SOW vs SLA", "How to write an MSA", and other Client Facing Document related questions. I wanted to use this post as a springboard on my philosophies on the SOW side and eventually I'll write some more on the other Documents you'd give a client. Whether you're a one person shop, project manager, or part of a MSP with a consulting arm, getting the SOW right can make or break a project. A clear SOW helps manage expectations, avoid scope creep, and ensures everyone is on the same page from day one. SOW Template Optimized for TurboDocx automation Example AWS Build SOW See a completed real-world example 1 Project Overview Although this is common sense, this section is all about defining what the project is and what the client is asking for. It's essential to set the tone and provide context. In the example I worked on, the client wanted us to build a web application and deploy it for five franchises. We also outlined that we'd evaluate the potential to expand this rollout to 2,500 franchises in the future. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER SOW Structure / Hierarchy Diagram Key Tip Make sure the overview clearly states what's included in the current phase and where future possibilities might lead. This helps prevent the annoying "But we thought this was included!" moment and lines you up for future work. 2 Scope Definition Here's where the magic happens . A good scope definition is clear and concise—it's the cornerstone of your SOW. In my project, we used Scope Tables to outline exactly what was in scope for the deployment, and specified that only the first five franchises were included. I also call out specifics like "3 US Regions" and give brief but concise bullet points on what's included. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER Scope Table Visualization " If it's not listed, it's not in scope. Best Practices Use clear, specific language—avoid vague terms Call out specific quantities and limitations (e.g., "5 franchises", "3 US Regions") 3 Out of Scope Critical Section Again - common sense, but one of the most critical sections of any SOW. It is what you're not going to do. Seriously, this can save you from so much scope creep. Example: What We Marked Out of Scope ❌ ❌ ❌ Any custom integrations beyond what's specified ❌ IMAGE PLACEHOLDER Scope Creep Prevention Visual Pro Tip Be super specific about what's not included. It helps prevent misunderstandings later and gives you room to negotiate additional services (and budgets!) if needed. For MSP/PS Shops with Enterprise Clients I would argue the next sections are for shops with enterprise styled clients, typically companies with a CIO or a company used to 5 figure+ engagements. I know some of the folks here service large brands and can relate to what I'm saying below... 4 Deliverables Clients love to know what they're getting for their money. In our SOW, we broke down the deliverables by phase: absolute -inset-0.5 bg-gradient-to-r rounded-2xl opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-20 blur transition-opacity Key Takeaway Make sure every deliverable is tied directly to the project's objectives. Vague deliverables like "provide support" won't cut it. 5 Project Management and Change Control Projects evolve. That's why a strong change management process is vital. We used a structured methodology for handling unexpected scope changes. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER Change Management Process Flowchart Calculate the effect on budget, timeline, and resources Why This Matters This process ensures that both parties agree before moving forward with additional work, avoiding disputes down the line. Back to regularly scheduled programming applying to everyone: 6 Assumptions You can't predict everything, but you can prepare. Outline general assumptions that are important for the project to succeed. Key Assumptions for Success The client's team will be available for regular meetings and questions Post-project agreement for ongoing services (or reference to MSA) Important Note If any assumptions are not met, this can lead to delays or increased costs. Having these documented gives you leverage if things go off track. 7 Estimated Fees Don't forget the financials! We estimated the total consulting fees and laid out clear guidelines for any changes in staffing or scope. Make sure to provide a breakdown of fees based on the project's phases and possible contingencies. Time and Material DEFINITION Billing based on actual work performed, tracked through timesheets or ongoing work logs. EXAMPLE Billing weekly for tasks such as feedback, remediation, or any variable tasks that arise as part of ongoing project support. PRACTICAL USE Useful for projects with uncertain scope or evolving requirements, where work effort and time may vary. Fixed Fee with Milestones DEFINITION Predetermined fees billed upon the completion of specific project phases or milestones, helping manage cash flow. EXAMPLE STRUCTURE Phase 1: Billing $5k upon completion of 'Assess Current Infrastructure' phase Phase 2: Billing $10k upon completion of 'AWS Cloud Build' phase Final: Remaining balance billed upon project completion PRACTICAL USE Effective for projects with well-defined phases, allowing clients to make payments incrementally as key objectives are met. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER Payment Milestone Timeline Visualization Project Closure Clause for Auto-Acceptance Purpose: To prevent project deadlock due to unresponsive clients, enabling project closure and final invoicing. SUGGESTED TEXT "The project will be considered closed upon the mutual acknowledgment of all deliverables as completed, or, if no response is received, within 4 weeks of work completion. This auto-acceptance clause prevents extended deadlock and allows timely revenue recognition." Final Thoughts A well-structured SOW is more than just a contract—it's a roadmap for success. Always remember to: Be crystal clear about what is and isn't included to prevent scope creep Document deliverables, assumptions, and payment terms upfront absolute -inset-0.5 bg-gradient-to-r rounded-2xl opacity-20 group-hover:opacity-30 blur transition-opacity I hope this breakdown helps you write better SOWs in your own projects. Curious to other people's thoughts and how they run shop. Excited to see how you can crank these SOWs out in seconds. @context https://schema.org @type Optimizing IT Workflow: A Guide to TurboDocx Templating Learn how to streamline your IT document creation with TurboDocx templating. Master creating templates, uploading documents, and optimizing your workflow for maximum efficiency. @type @type @type https://www.turbodocx.com/TDAILogo.svg https://www.turbodocx.com/images/blog/it-workflow-banner.jpg https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/optimizing-it-workflow-a-guide-to-turbodocx-templating @type @id https://www.turbodocx.com/blog/optimizing-it-workflow-a-guide-to-turbodocx-templating IT workflow, document automation, TurboDocx, templating, productivity, IT management Best Practices Optimizing IT Workflow: A Guide to TurboDocx Templating By TurboDocx Team • June 8th, 2024 • 5 min read In IT, efficiency is everything. TurboDocx is a powerful tool that can streamline your document creation, making your workflow smoother and more consistent. This guide will show you how to get started with TurboDocx, from setting up your first template to using its advanced features. Whether you're an IT manager or a developer, learn how TurboDocx can save you time and reduce errors in your documentation process. Dive in and discover the benefits of optimizing your IT workflow with TurboDocx! Here are the steps to make you the master of creating your own template. 1 Create a New Template Open your preferred document application (Word, Google Docs, etc.). Identify the variables or items that will change from document to document and place them between these {brackets} . These can be individual items like {Date} or {CustomerName} , or entire sections like {Scope} . After inserting all the necessary variables, save your document. 2 Upload the Template Document Log in to your TurboDocx account and navigate to the Templates tab (located on the left side if you're not there by default). Click the "New Template" button at the top right of the window. Select the "Upload Template" option and choose the document you saved in the previous step, or simply drag and drop the file into the upload area. 3 Preview the Template You will now see a preview of your template. Ensure all the variables are correctly listed in the variables column. Optionally, you can set default entries for your variables on this page, which can be changed later when creating the final document. Once everything is verified, click the "Create Template" button at the bottom right corner of the screen (you might need to scroll down to see it). You're Ready to Go! By following these simple steps, you have now mastered the basics of creating and uploading templates in TurboDocx. This powerful tool will significantly streamline your document creation process, ensuring consistency and efficiency in your workflow. With your templates set up, you'll save time, reduce errors, and improve the overall quality of your documentation. Keep exploring TurboDocx's features to further optimize your IT tasks and enhance your productivity. Happy templating!

# TurboDocx Writer now Available on Microsoft AppSource

## Key Features of TurboDocx Writer:

## Looking Ahead: Enhancing Microsoft Office with AI Capabilities

### About TurboDocx

Back to Newsroom Product Launch October 1st, 2024 TurboDocx Writer now Available on Microsoft AppSource Bringing Advanced Document Automation to Microsoft Word Jupiter, FL – October 1, 2024 – TurboDocx, a leading provider of AI-powered document generation solutions, is excited to announce that its revolutionary new Word Plugin, TurboDocx Writer, is now available for install directly from Microsoft AppSource. This new integration empowers users to harness the full power of TurboDocx's advanced templating, variable replacement, and content injection capabilities directly within Microsoft Word, enabling faster, smarter, and more efficient document creation workflows. TurboDocx Writer is designed to streamline document generation processes for professionals across industries. Users can now create, update, and personalize documents effortlessly, utilizing TurboDocx's intuitive point-and-click interface to insert dynamic content from a knowledgebase, templates, or custom data sources—without ever leaving Word. By seamlessly integrating into one of the most popular word processing platforms, TurboDocx Writer makes document automation accessible to a wide audience, including legal teams, sales departments, MSPs, and professional service providers. Key Features of TurboDocx Writer: Point-and-Click Simplicity: Easily inject dynamic content into your documents with just a few clicks. Full Template Integration: Utilize pre-built or custom templates to populate documents quickly and accurately. Advanced Variable Replacement: Automatically swap out placeholders with real-time data, ensuring consistent and error-free content. Seamless Integration with Microsoft Word: Enjoy the familiar Word experience enhanced by TurboDocx's robust automation features. "We are thrilled to bring TurboDocx Writer to Microsoft AppSource, enabling users to leverage our powerful document automation tools right within the Microsoft Office ecosystem," said Nicolas Fry, Founder and CEO of TurboDocx. "With this plugin, professionals can reduce manual work, eliminate copy-paste errors, and focus more on the content that truly matters to their business. We're proud to continue making document automation more accessible and efficient for users everywhere." Looking Ahead: Enhancing Microsoft Office with AI Capabilities As TurboDocx continues to innovate, we are committed to further enhancing Microsoft Office with AI-driven capabilities. Our roadmap includes deeper integration with Microsoft's evolving AI features, allowing users to not only automate document creation but also leverage intelligent suggestions, smart insights, and contextual enhancements across Word and other Office applications. TurboDocx aims to transform the way businesses interact with their documents, bringing even greater flexibility, accuracy, and intelligence to the entire Microsoft Office experience. Revolutionizing the Way You Create and Reuse Content TurboDocx is an AI-assisted document and slide deck templating platform designed to empower professionals to build documents quickly by eliminating tedious copy-pasting and leveraging AI. Our Story TurboDocx was born from challenges faced by consulting and sales professionals who spent excessive time creating presentations and documentation. We started with simple text swaps, evolved to a robust content "building blocks" engine, and eventually integrated AI capabilities to enhance content creation. # Privacy Policy

## 12. Contact Us

Back to Legal Documents Privacy Policy Last Modified: April 2nd, 2025 This Privacy Policy describes how TURBODOCX, INC. ("we", "us", or "our") collects, uses, and protects your personal information when you use www.TurboDocx.com and our related services. 1. Information We Collect We may collect the following types of information: Personal Details: Name, email address, phone number, and company information Content: Documents, templates, and other content you create or upload Usage Information: How you interact with our platform, features used, and activity logs Website Access Data: IP address, browser type, device information, and access times Customer Support Data: Records of your communications with our support team Third-Party Platform Data: Information from connected services like Google or social media Payment Information: Billing details processed securely via Stripe or Paddle 2. Lawful Basis for Data Processing We process your data based on: Your consent Performance of our contract with you Compliance with legal obligations Protection of vital interests Public interest Our legitimate business interests 3. How We Use Your Information We use collected information to: Provide and improve our services Create and deliver your requested documents Process payments and manage subscriptions Personalize your experience Send marketing communications (with your consent) Provide technical support and troubleshooting Comply with legal requirements Detect and prevent fraud 4. Third-Party Data Sharing We may share your data with trusted service providers including: Cloud Infrastructure: AWS, Microsoft Azure Authentication: Auth0 AI Services: OpenAI, Google Payment Processing: Stripe, Paddle Analytics: Google Analytics Communication: Email service providers We require all third parties to maintain appropriate security measures and only process your data according to our instructions. 5. Your Rights You have the right to: Access your personal information Request correction of inaccurate data Request deletion of your data Opt-out of data collection Withdraw consent at any time Data portability Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority 6. Data Security We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your personal information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. This includes encryption, access controls, and regular security assessments. 7. Data Retention We retain your personal information only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected, or as required by law. When data is no longer needed, we securely delete or anonymize it. 8. Cookies and Tracking We use cookies and similar technologies to enhance your experience, analyze usage patterns, and deliver personalized content. You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings. 9. Children's Privacy Our services are not directed to individuals under 16. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we learn we have collected such information, we will take steps to delete it. 10. International Data Transfers Your information may be transferred to and processed in countries other than your own. We ensure appropriate safeguards are in place for such transfers, including standard contractual clauses. 11. Changes to This Policy We may update this Privacy Policy periodically. We will notify you of material changes by posting the updated policy on our website with a new effective date. 12. Contact Us If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or our data practices, please contact us: TURBODOCX, INC. Jupiter, FL Email: privacy@turbodocx.com Copyright © TurboDocx, Inc. All rights reserved.
